sentences.text:
Present petition has been filed by the Petitioner under Section 482 Cr.P.C. for quashing of FIR No.
173/2018 dated 27.04.2018 under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC, P.S. Shakarpur, Delhi and consequential proceedings emanating therefrom.
2. Issue notice.
3. Learned APP accepts notice on behalf of the State.

4. Mr. Harshit Shishodia, learned counsel accepts notice on behalf of Respondent No. 2.
5.
Marriage between Petitioner and Respondent No. 2 was solemnized on 20.04.2003 according to Hindu rites and ceremonies.
Two children are born out of the said wedlock and both are presently living with the Petitioner.

sentences.text: On account of temperamental differences, parties have been living separately since 05.02.2017.
On a complaint filed by Respondent No. 2 against the Petitioner and other family members, the present FIR was lodged.
Charge sheet has been filed against the Petitioner only while the other family members are kept in Column No. 12.

In the interregnum, on intervention of common friends and relatives, parties have amicably resolved their inter se disputes and terms of settlement have been incorporated in a Settlement Deed executed on 20.09.2022 copy of which has been annexed to the present petition.
Marriage between the parties has been dissolved by a Decree of Divorce by mutual consent and copy of the decree sheet dated 28.11.2022 is on record.

Additionally, both parties have filed their respective affidavits stating that the settlement arrived at between the parties will not come in the way of both the children exercising their future rights in accordance with law against the parties.

As per the Settlement Deed, Petitioner agreed to pay a sum of Rs.5,00,000/- to Respondent No.2 out of which Rs.4,00,000/- stands paid while the balance amount was payable at the time of quashing of the FIR.
It was further agreed that all pending cases filed by the parties against each other will be withdrawn before filing the quashing petition, amongst other terms.
7. Petitioner and Respondent No. 2 are present in Court and are identified by their respective counsels and Investigating Officer SI Vijay Dutt, PS: Laxmi Nagar.

Respondent No. 2 states that terms of settlement have been complied with and she has no objection to the FIR being quashed to put a quietus to the litigations between the parties and to maintain peace and harmony as well as in the interest of the children.
Learned APP

8. In the context of exercise of inherent powers under Section 482 Cr.P.C., while dealing with matrimonial disputes, the Supreme Court in Jitendra Raghuvanshi and Others v. Babita Raghuvanshi and Another, (2013) 4 SCC 58, held as follows:-
"15.

entities.text: Jitendra Raghuvanshi and Others v. Babita Raghuvanshi and Another, (2013) 4 SCC 58
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In our view, it is the duty of the courts to encourage genuine settlements of matrimonial disputes, particularly, when the same are on considerable increase.
Even if the offences are non- compoundable, if they relate to matrimonial disputes and the Court is satisfied that the parties have settled the same amicably and without any pressure
, we hold that for the purpose of securing ends of justice, Section 320 of the Code would not be a bar to the exercise of power of quashing of FIR, complaint or the subsequent criminal proceedings.
16. There has been an outburst of matrimonial disputes in recent times.
The institution of marriage occupies an important place and it has an important role to play in the society.
Therefore, every effort should be made in the interest of the individuals in order to enable them to settle down in life and live peacefully.

If the parties ponder over their defaults and terminate their disputes amicably by mutual agreement instead of fighting it out in a court of law, in order to do complete justice Giriraj Gupta vs State (Govt Of Nct Of Delhi) & Anr on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155228233/
2 in the matrimonial matters, the courts should be less hesitant in exercising their extraordinary jurisdiction.

entities.text: Giriraj Gupta vs State (Govt Of Nct Of Delhi) & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is trite to state that the power under Section 482 should be exercised sparingly and with circumspection only when the Court is convinced, on the basis of material on record, that allowing the proceedings to continue would be an abuse of process of court or that the ends of justice require that the proceedings ought to be quashed.

We also make it clear that exercise of such power would depend upon the facts and circumstances of each case and it has to be exercised in appropriate cases in order to do real and substantial justice for the administration of which alone the courts exist.

It is the duty of the courts to encourage genuine settlements of matrimonial disputes and Section 482 of the Code enables the High Court and Article 142 of the Constitution enables this Court to pass such orders."
9. In view of the settlement between the parties, this Court finds no impediment in quashing the present FIR.

sentences.text: Accordingly, FIR No. 173/2018 under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC, P.S. Shakarpur, Delhi is quashed including all proceedings emanating therefrom.

It is however made clear that in view of the judgment of the Supreme Court in Ganesh v.
Sudhirkumar Shrivastava and others, (2020) 20 SCC 787, the settlement arrived at between the parties shall not come in the way of the two children enforcing their rights available in law, if and when required and to this extent the parties shall be bound by the undertakings given in the affidavits referred to above.
10. Petition stands allowed and disposed of in the aforesaid terms.
JYOTI SINGH, J NOVEMBER 16, 2023/
